item.title: She Vanished At A Hotel Party And Was Found In A Freezer
item.description: Nineteen-year-old Kenneka Jenkins disappeared after attending a party at a Rosemont, Illinois, hotel in September 2017. Surveillance footage showed her wandering alone through the hotel before she was found dead inside a walk-in freezer. The medical examiner ruled her death accidental, caused by hypothermia with alcohol and medication contributing, but questions surrounding her final hours continue to fuel debate.

item.title: Charles Manson: The Cult Leader Behind A Bloody Nightmare
item.description: Charles Manson built a devoted following known as the Manson Family before his followers carried out a series of murders in Los Angeles in 1969, including the killings at Sharon Tate's home. Manson was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy and became one of America's most infamous cult leaders.

item.title: Did His Water-Powered Car Get Him Killed?
item.description: Stanley Meyer claimed he had developed a revolutionary water-fuel cell that could power a car, but his death in 1998 sparked a lasting conspiracy theory that he was poisoned to silence his invention. Investigators found no evidence of foul play, and the coroner ruled that Meyer died from a ruptured cerebral aneurysm.

item.title: The Tragic Murder Of Vanessa Guillén
item.description: U.S. Army Specialist Vanessa Guillén disappeared from Fort Hood in April 2020, triggering a massive search and national outrage. Investigators determined that fellow soldier Aaron Robinson killed her, while his girlfriend Cecily Aguilar helped conceal her remains. The case also exposed serious failures in the Army's handling of sexual harassment and accountability.

item.title: He Died During A Fraternity Hazing Ritual
item.description: Eighteen-year-old Gordie Bailey died of acute alcohol poisoning in 2004 after a Chi Psi fraternity hazing event at the University of Colorado Boulder. He and other pledges were pressured to consume enormous amounts of alcohol in a short time, and he was later left unconscious for hours. His death became a landmark case in the fight against fraternity hazing.

item.title: She Vanished In Just 13 Minutes And Was Never Seen Again
item.description: Patrice Endres disappeared from her Georgia hair salon during a baffling 13-minute window on April 15, 2004. Her remains were discovered 20 months later, but more than two decades on, no one has been charged with her murder. Investigators are still seeking answers and recently renewed their appeal for information.

item.title: The Boyfriend Who Died After A Disturbing Texting Scheme
item.description: Eighteen-year-old Conrad Roy died from carbon monoxide poisoning in 2014 after a long struggle with depression. Investigators later uncovered messages showing his girlfriend, Michelle Carter, repeatedly encouraged him to follow through with his suicide, and she was ultimately convicted of involuntary manslaughter and sentenced to 15 months in prison

item.title: She Was Released Alone Then Vanished Into The Night
item.description: Mitrice Richardson was released from a Los Angeles County sheriff's station shortly after midnight in September 2009 without her car, phone, or wallet. She disappeared hours later, and her remains were found nearly a year later in Malibu Canyon. The medical examiner could not determine how she died, leaving her family still seeking answers.
